question: For a four-leg intersection evaluated under the one-year Crash Experience signal warrant, what crash thresholds apply and what two additional categories of conditions must also be satisfied?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Under Warrant 7 (Crash Experience), a four-leg intersection meets the one-year crash criterion if reported angle and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equal or exceed the threshold number in Table 4C-2 — either for total angle and pedestrian crashes (all severities) or for total fatal-and-injury angle and pedestrian crashes (the specific numeric values in Table 4C-2 are not included in the evidence provided). In addition to the crash-history condition, two other categories of conditions must be satisfied: (A) an adequate trial of alternatives with satisfactory observance and enforcement has failed to reduce crash frequency, and (C) a traffic-volume condition applying for each of any 8 hours of an average day (the full text of this volume condition is truncated in the evidence). Guidance (recommended): - The need for a traffic control signal should be considered if an engineering study finds that all of the following criteria are met: "A. Adequate trial of alternatives with satisfactory observance and enforcement has failed to reduce the crash frequency." - Crash-history condition (at least one must apply): "1. The number of reported angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total angle crashes and pedestrian crashes (all severities); or 2. The number of reported fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes within a 1-year period equals or exceeds the threshold number in Table 4C-2 for total fatal-and-injury angle crashes and pedestrian crashes." - A third criterion (C) requires a condition to be met "For each of any 8 hours of an average day"; the remainder of this volume-related provision is cut off in the supplied evidence. Options (permitted): - If the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed on the major street exceeds 40 mph, or the intersection lies within the built-up area of an isolated community of less than 10,000 population, Table 4C-4 may be used in place of Table 4C-2 (and the 56 percent volume columns in Table 4C-1 may be used in place of the 80 percent columns). - Agencies may calibrate HSM safety performance functions to their own crash data, or develop their own SPFs, and when documented in the engineering study these agency-specific crash frequency values may be used instead of the values in Tables 4C-2 through 4C-5. Citations: - Section 4C.08 Guidance §2 (p.661) - Section 4C.08 Option §5 (p.662) - Section 4C.08 Option §6 (p.663) - Section 4C.08 Support §1 (p.661) - Section 4C.08 Support §7 (p.663) Note: The evidence does not include the actual numeric threshold values from Table 4C-2, and the text of criterion C (the 8-hour traffic-volume condition) is truncated, so those details cannot be quoted in full. (The crash figures in Section 2B.11 pertain to minor-road stop control, not the Crash Experience signal warrant, and are therefore not applicable here.)
gold_answer: The thresholds are at least 5 all-severity angle/pedestrian crashes or at least 3 fatal-and-injury angle/pedestrian crashes. In addition, an adequate trial of alternatives must have failed, and the applicable 80-percent vehicular-volume or pedestrian-volume condition must be met for the required hours.
